title: SEMICON West's Autonomous Fab Vision Needs a Decision-Escalation Design
gist: Behavioral scientist Gleb Tsipursky argues that SEMICON West's autonomous-fab push needs explicit decision-escalation design before AI agents get operational authority. He proposes permission boundaries, traceable handoffs, tested exception paths, decision-level metrics, and workforce practices that keep engineers' judgment sharp.

insights.claim: SEMICON West 2026's smart-manufacturing agenda linked digital twins, agentic AI, physical AI and increasingly autonomous factory operations, and PDF Solutions planned October CONNECT demonstrations of Exensio Aurora for agentic AI across fab operations and the supply chain.
insights.speaker: Gleb Tsipursky
insights.so_what: Shows investment direction toward agentic AI in fabs.

insights.claim: Product specifications and conference demonstrations do not establish performance inside a production fab, so the practical question is when an AI recommendation becomes an authorized action and who is accountable.
insights.speaker: Gleb Tsipursky
insights.so_what: Discount vendor demos until production results exist.
insights.locator: These announcements indicate the direction of investment

insights.claim: An AI-found correlation between an equipment signal and yield may justify further investigation in exploratory analysis, but on a live line it cannot automatically justify a process-setting change because the cause could be an instrument issue, unusual material lot, maintenance event or a real process shift.
insights.speaker: Gleb Tsipursky
insights.so_what: Correlation-driven automation risks false process changes in the fab.
insights.locator: An AI system might identify a correlation

insights.claim: Fab leaders should design decision-escalation rules into workflows before granting an agent operational authority.
insights.speaker: Gleb Tsipursky
insights.so_what: Governance is a precondition for deploying agentic AI in fabs.
insights.locator: Fab leaders should therefore design decision-escalation

insights.claim: Permission boundaries should separate agents that retrieve records and draft explanations from those allowed to initiate holds, propose parameter changes or alter tool instructions; a general promise to keep humans in the loop offers little without specified decisions, reviewers, evidence and permissible autonomy.
insights.speaker: Gleb Tsipursky
insights.so_what: Tiered authority is the practical control for agentic fab systems.

insights.claim: Every handoff should be traceable: the process engineer should see source data, affected tools or lots, uncertainties and intended effect, with a record of who reviewed what and whether the suggestion was accepted, because a fluent explanation should never replace the traceable record.
insights.speaker: Gleb Tsipursky
insights.so_what: Audit trails will be a required feature of fab AI products.

insights.claim: Exception paths should be created during testing, covering missing telemetry, contradictory indicators, a tool returning from maintenance, unusual material lots and an apparent improvement followed by a downstream quality problem, with decisions on which exceptions suspend automation or need a second reviewer.
insights.speaker: Gleb Tsipursky
insights.so_what: Edge-case handling distinguishes robust deployments from demos.
insights.locator: Create the exception path during testing.

insights.claim: Organizations should measure decisions rather than dashboard activity, tracking time to investigate anomalies, recommendations reversed after review, repeat exceptions and engineering hours spent verifying suggestions, since faster analysis can slow operations by shifting hidden verification work onto engineers.
insights.speaker: Gleb Tsipursky
insights.so_what: ROI of fab AI depends on net engineering time and yield, not speed of analysis.
insights.locator: Then measure decisions rather than dashboard activity.

insights.claim: Experienced process engineers may question opaque recommendations because they have seen plausible correlations fail under changing conditions, and should be given a formal role in building test cases and defining stop rules.
insights.speaker: Gleb Tsipursky
insights.so_what: Skeptical domain experts improve deployment safety.

insights.claim: If an agent supplies the apparent diagnosis first, junior engineers may get fewer chances to practice reasoning needed when the system is wrong, so structured reviews where they defend explanations before seeing the agent's output should be preserved.
insights.speaker: Gleb Tsipursky
insights.so_what: AI deskilling risk in fab engineering talent pipelines.
insights.locator: Junior engineers face a different risk.

insights.claim: For any agent-initiated action leaders should be able to answer what evidence supported it, who could stop or override it, and how they will know whether the decision improved performance.
insights.speaker: Gleb Tsipursky
insights.so_what: Three-question test for evaluating autonomous-fab deployments.
insights.locator: The CONNECT 2026 agenda demonstrates the growing commercial focus
